clue.text: Seaman posted as missing

blocks.note: a letter posted has been sent

explanation.surface: A sailor has been officially listed as missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is absent is not present, just as a missing person is nowhere to be found.

clue.text: Sit up following a storyteller

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading the word from the bottom, so backwards

blocks.note: to sit for an artist is to pose

explanation.surface: Children sit up straight as a storyteller begins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following a' places the reversed word after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop was the ancient Greek teller of fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Lady's maid bringing new berets out

indicators.note: a new version of something is a remade one, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A maid unpacks some fresh berets for her mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A soubrette is a stock comedy role: a pert, flirtatious lady's maid in opera or theatre.

clue.text: Gets gen about savings

indicators.note: turned about suggests moving things around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone gathers information about their savings.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: A nest egg is money put aside for the future, an idiom for a sum of savings.

clue.text: Harridan therefore sent back on vessel

indicators.note: something sent back returns the way it came, so the word is read from right to left

explanation.surface: A nagging woman is packed off on a ship as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'A on B' puts A before B.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, belligerent old woman, and an ogress is a fearsome female monster, a figurative synonym.

clue.text: Interrogate, about ring, a thug

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word is wrapped round the next piece

blocks.note: to grill someone is to question them hard

explanation.surface: A thug is questioned about a ring of criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorilla is informal for a big brutish man employed for muscle, a thug.

clue.text: Painter from southern state

indicators.note: taken from within the following words, the letters run across the word break

blocks.note: found inside these words, across the gap

explanation.surface: An artist hailing from one of the southern US states.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German-born Surrealist painter.

clue.text: Replace wonderful watch set with diamonds

indicators.note: a jewel set in a mounting is held within it, so one piece goes inside another

explanation.surface: Swapping a fine wristwatch for one encrusted with diamonds.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to take its place, so it means replace.

clue.text: Fruit belonging to us included in bribe

indicators.note: one thing included in another sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a sop is something given to pacify or buy off
what belongs to us is ours

explanation.surface: A sweetener slipped to someone happens to be our own fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The soursop is a tropical fruit with spiny green skin and soft white flesh.

clue.text: Instruments producing different pair of notes

definitions.text: Instruments producing different pair of notes

blocks.clueFragment: Instruments producing different pair of notes
blocks.note: surface reading: devices that play two distinct musical tones

blocks.clueFragment: Instruments producing different pair of notes
blocks.note: setter's reading: keyboards named for producing both soft and loud notes, the Italian dynamic markings

explanation.walkthrough: The full name of the keyboard instrument joins the Italian words for soft and loud, two contrasting kinds of note it can play.
explanation.definitionFit: The full name means soft-loud, because hammers let players vary volume, unlike the harpsichord.

clue.text: Vegetable cut, cut and cut again

indicators.note: the second cut acts on the first, trimming the end off the word it gives

blocks.note: to pare is to cut away the outer layer
to snip is to cut with scissors

explanation.surface: A cook keeps chopping a root vegetable into ever smaller pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: The three cuts do three jobs: a word, an instruction to shorten it, and a second word.
explanation.definitionFit: The parsnip is a pale root vegetable related to the carrot.

clue.text: Fast mail service could be £25, say

blocks.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds
to express something is to say it

explanation.surface: A quick courier service might cost twenty-five pounds, say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example' but supplies a word of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pony Express was the 1860s American mail service relaying riders on horseback across the West.

clue.text: Other ranks put in awful place in China?

indicators.note: an awful arrangement is a bad one, so these letters need reordering
things put in something end up inside it

blocks.note: OR, other ranks: soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: Common soldiers are posted somewhere dreadful in the country of China.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital C hides the lower-case meaning: china is crockery, not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Porcelain is the fine ceramic commonly called china, after the country where it was first made.

clue.text: Following behind, close to mother

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is kept

explanation.surface: Someone trails along at the heels of their mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and following both describe something that comes after, as in the following or later day.

clue.text: Be a role model giving group a suitable warning

blocks.note: a punishment made an example of serves as a warning to others

explanation.surface: A mentor shows a group a fitting cautionary tale.
explanation.definitionFit: To set a good example is to behave in a way others should copy, which is what a role model does.

clue.text: A bassinet, possibly for Alonso's brother

indicators.note: possibly signals one of several possible arrangements, so these letters can be reordered

explanation.surface: A baby's cot might do for Alonso's younger sibling.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's The Tempest, Sebastian is the brother of Alonso, King of Naples.

clue.text: Ralph and Enid unwisely flirt

indicators.note: acting unwisely is acting wrongly, so these letters fall out of order

blocks.note: letters of the two names, rearranged; the joining word is not used

explanation.surface: Two people foolishly carry on a flirtation.
explanation.definitionFit: To philander is to have casual love affairs, so to flirt with many partners.

clue.text: Suit's failure to fulfil an engagement?

definitions.text: Suit's failure to fulfil an engagement?

blocks.clueFragment: Suit's failure to fulfil an engagement?
blocks.note: surface reading: a businessman in a suit fails to turn up to an appointment

blocks.clueFragment: Suit's failure to fulfil an engagement?
blocks.note: setter's reading: a lawsuit brought because someone broke off a promise to marry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' suggests a business type, and 'engagement' an appointment; here they are a legal action and a betrothal.
explanation.definitionFit: Breach of promise was a civil action for damages against a person who broke an agreement to marry.

clue.text: Skipper, international, leading reserves at home

blocks.note: a cap is awarded for playing for your country, and a player capped is an international
TA, Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force

explanation.surface: A team skipper, an international player, leads the reserves in a home match.
explanation.walkthrough: In British sport an international player is called a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the captain of a team or ship, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Opening of poem about gold and diamonds? Just the opposite

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is wrapped round another
this flips the instruction just given, so the outer and inner pieces swap places

explanation.surface: The first lines of a poem about gold and gems, or so it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just the opposite' reverses the instruction: the gold and diamonds go around the poem, not the poem around them.
explanation.definitionFit: An orifice is a hole or opening, especially in the body.

clue.text: Small musical instrument, piercing

blocks.note: S, small, as in clothing sizes
the harp is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A little instrument with a shrill, piercing tone.
explanation.definitionFit: Sharp and piercing both describe something with a fine point, or a shrill sound or keen pain.

clue.text: In fact, Edith Evans did

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit within the following words

blocks.note: found inside these words, across the comma

explanation.surface: The famous actress Edith Evans really did perform.
explanation.walkthrough: Dame Edith Evans was a celebrated English stage actress, so the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acted is a past tense like did: acting is doing, and an actress like Evans acted on stage.

clue.text: Article on reptile leaving peninsula

explanation.surface: A newspaper item about a reptile departing from a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: THE LIZARD is the Cornish peninsula at the southernmost tip of mainland Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lizard is a named peninsula in Cornwall, England, so it is an example of the class.

clue.text: Material excavated from below

indicators.note: in a down clue reading from below means starting at the bottom, so backwards

explanation.surface: Cloth dug up from beneath the ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a tough cotton twill fabric, the cloth of jeans.

clue.text: Sit near suspect, crying

indicators.note: a suspect account is not to be trusted as it stands, so these letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Someone weeping is told to sit beside a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in tears is to be weeping, an idiom for crying.

clue.text: Boy catching breath in town

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: to get your wind back is to recover your breath

explanation.surface: A lad pausing to catch his breath somewhere in town.
explanation.walkthrough: SWINDON is a large town in Wiltshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Swindon is a railway town in southern England, an example of a town.

clue.text: French girl, one under ten, fixing plug

indicators.note: something fixing in place is fastened inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a plug is a piece of advertising, an ad

explanation.surface: A French child under ten is repairing an electric plug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One under ten' looks like the letter I below TEN; it is simply the number below ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadine is a girl's name of French origin.

clue.text: Take out retired National winner

indicators.note: something retired has withdrawn back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to take someone out is to kill them

explanation.surface: A former Grand National champion, now retired, is withdrawn from service.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase; Red Rum won it three times in the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Rum is the racehorse famous for winning the Grand National in 1973, 1974 and 1977.
